Closes #36. Enforce model-origin exclusions in the router, not only in eval policy.

## Why
`[routing] exclude_origins` in config.toml is parsed today only by `src/evals/settings.ts` and honoured only by `src/evals/policy.ts` (a model is excluded when its `origin` or `baseOrigin` is listed, or when its `baseOrigin` is "unknown" while a list is configured). The runtime `Router` (src/router/router.ts) ignores it, so when subscription quotas ran out, review and verify calls fell back to a CN-origin model even though the policy work assumed such models were excluded. At work, CN-origin models must never be called.

## What
1. One shared parser for `[routing] exclude_origins` (reuse it in `evalSettings`; the semantics above stay identical, including "unknown baseOrigin is excluded when a list is configured"). No exclusion when the key is absent (today's behaviour at home stays unchanged).
2. The Router treats an excluded model as ineligible on every route: policy cells, out-of-cell fallbacks, the free-first and vendor-avoidance fallbacks, escalation, panel and verifier selection, and models added at runtime (`catalog add`, discovery). The skip reason in the run log and in `routing preview` reads `origin excluded (<origin>; baseOrigin=<baseOrigin>)`. There is NO fallback to an excluded model: when exclusions leave no candidate, the invocation fails with that reason.
3. Explicit choices are refused up front, never silently skipped: `run --model role=…` and `retry --model`, `routing set`, the Setup tab's routing and fallback saves (HTTP 400 with the reason), `catalog add` of an excluded origin (allowed to add, but `catalog list` marks it excluded and routing never picks it), and `eval run --models` (refuses excluded models with the reason before any trial starts).
4. Visibility: `routing show`, `catalog list` and the Setup tab show the configured exclusions (read-only; changing them stays a config.toml edit plus restart, on purpose: it is a safety constraint).
5. Docs: document the key and its semantics where routing config is documented.

## Tests (fake harness only; read test/AGENTS.md)
- A fallback that would reach an excluded model when every allowed provider is exhausted fails with the reason instead (this is the regression).
- Each refusal path above (run pin, retry pin, routing set, HTTP setup save, eval run) rejects an excluded model; a model whose baseOrigin is "unknown" is excluded only when a list is configured.
- With no `exclude_origins`, routing is byte-for-byte unchanged (existing routing tests keep passing).

Budget: about 200 changed source lines plus tests. Out of scope: per-repo or per-role exclusion lists, live editing of the list.

The repository's own factory test gate already allows 1,800 s (\`.limitless.toml\`); this aligns the deploy gate with it. Lint and typecheck keep 10 minutes.

## Problem
When a CI job hits its workflow `timeout-minutes`, GitHub cancels it, and the job's log is never uploaded. `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/actions/jobs/{id}/logs` then returns 404 (`BlobNotFound`). The CI classifier (`src/integrations/ci-classifier.ts`) downloads the log of every failed job that started. The GitHub poller's generic handling turns any 404 into an access problem (`accessProblem` in `src/integrations/github-poller.ts`: "The gh token cannot see <repo>"). So the classifier emits `github.access_problem` and stops, and it never reaches its own rule that reruns a `cancelled` or `timed_out` job once.

This happened twice on 2026-10-08, on factory PRs #408 (run 37725010065) and #415 (run 37725905014). Each emitted `pr.ci_failed`, then `github.access_problem` (reason `not_found`) although the token could read the repository and the rate limits were full. Neither job was rerun until the orchestrator reran it by hand, and both reruns passed. This affects any repository whose CI job can time out.

## Change
1. In the classifier, a 404 on the log of a job it has just read counts as "log unavailable", not as an access problem. Classification continues without the log, so a `cancelled` or `timed_out` job is still transient and gets its one rerun under the existing rules. Keep this narrow: a 404 on the repository, the PR, the run or the job itself is still an access problem.
2. Record in the failure (signature or line) that the log was unavailable, so a later `ci.needs_fix` says so instead of quoting nothing.

## Tests (fake `gh` fixtures)
- A cancelled job after `timeout-minutes` whose log endpoint returns 404 gets exactly one rerun and emits no `github.access_problem`. If the rerun times out the same way, the result is `ci.needs_fix` noting the missing log, with no second rerun.
- A 404 on the PR or the repository still emits `github.access_problem` with reason `not_found`.
- A job log that returns 200 is classified exactly as before.

## Budget
About 20 net source lines, plus tests.

## Out of scope
- Making this repository's hung CI runs visible (#416).
- Changing the rerun policy.

## Problem
Inside confinement, every zsh here-document fails with `zsh:1: can't create temp file for here document: operation not permitted`. zsh writes here-document temp files under `TMPPREFIX`, which defaults to `<tmp>`, and confined commands can't write the system temp directories (by design; AGENTS.md says not to hardcode `/tmp`). Agents on this Mac run their shell commands in zsh (`/bin/zsh -lc ...`), so any here-doc they write (`cat <<EOF`, `python3 - <<'PY'`) fails, and they lose turns working around it. The message appears repeatedly in recent runs' event logs (for example run <run-id> on 2026-10-08).

- default: `zsh -lc 'cat <<EOF ...'` → exit 1, the error above;
- `TMPPREFIX="$TMPDIR/zsh"`, set by `export` inside the command or through the environment → exit 0, the here-doc works (a login shell's profile doesn't override it).

Wherever the factory points `TMPDIR` at a run's or command's private scratch, also set `TMPPREFIX` to a path inside that same scratch (for example `<scratch>/zsh`): `runConfined` in `src/harness/sandbox.ts` and the environments of the Codex and Claude agent invocations. ## Problem
Two tests in `test/land-queue.test.ts` fail intermittently on Linux CI with one extra entry in the fake gate's log right after the queue stops:
- "stopping mid-check leaves a later entry unstarted" (PR #433's CI, 2026-10-08), `expect(gateLog()).toEqual(["start"])` at line 581;
- "a restart during checking re-runs the checks from the start" (PR #439's CI, run 37886446828, 2026-10-09), the same assertion at line 647.

The fake land check is `echo start >> gates.log; sleep 0.3; echo end >> gates.log` (line 76). Both tests wait until "start" appears, call `stop()`, and assert the log is still `["start"]`, so they assume `stop()` interrupts the check within 0.3 s of the poll that saw "start". On a loaded runner the poll interval plus stop latency can exceed that, the check writes "end", and the assertion fails. This is a timing assumption in the test, not a land-queue defect: the tests' later assertions show a stopped check is re-run from the start.

## Change
Make the fake check wait for an explicit release instead of a fixed sleep: for example `echo start >> gates.log; while [ ! -e release ]; do sleep 0.05; done; echo end >> gates.log`, with the tests that need checks to finish creating the release file (immediately, or at the point they currently rely on the sleep). The two stop tests keep the check unreleased until after `stop()`, so "end" can only appear if `stop()` failed to interrupt it. Keep each test's other assertions as they are.

## Tests
- The two tests pass, and fail if `stop()` stops interrupting a running check (check by temporarily making `stop()` wait for the check to finish).
- The other land-queue tests still pass with the release mechanism, without longer timeouts.

## Budget
Test-only, about 30 lines.

## Out of scope
- Changing the land queue's stop or resume behavior.
- Raising timeouts or retrying tests.

## What happened
Linux CI failed on the landing queue's base merge for #451 (run 38034887488, 2026-10-10):

```

test/failure-injection.test.ts:1373  expect(pids.size).toBe(2)  Expected: 2  Received: 0
```

#451 doesn't touch delivery, and this is the first occurrence in the last 25 failed CI runs.

## Cause
In the `comments` case, the fake `gh api` blocks and writes `delivery-pids` during the first factory's delivery. The test then runs `settled` and `reopen(f)`. Stopping the first factory kills that blocked `gh api` and its `sleep`, but the file stays.

After the restart, `await wait(() => existsSync(pidFile))` returns at once on the old file. Whether `retainPids` sees live pids then depends on whether the reopened factory's delivery has already overwritten the file: here it hadn't, so both pids were dead.

## Change
Remove `delivery-pids` before `reopen(f)` in the `comments` case, so the wait observes the reopened factory's process. Change nothing else in the test.

## Test
- The test passes 20 times in a row under `bun test --parallel=4` with `test/failure-injection.test.ts` alone.
- Without the change, show the race: with a short sleep injected between `reopen` and the read (in a scratch copy, not committed), the test gets 0 pids.

## Budget
A few lines in `test/failure-injection.test.ts` only.

The other cases and the file's barriers.

Follow-up from #458's review. It ships before CI fix rounds, which will add a new `review_rounds.kind`.

## Change
1. **Readers tolerate an unknown round kind.** `validateRoundKind` (`src/db/store.ts`) throws on any kind other than `review` or `conflict`, and `reviewRounds` runs it on every row. A rollback from a release that writes a new kind would therefore make every round read for that PR throw. Instead:
   - an unknown kind is kept as data;
   - it counts as in flight for the one-round-per-PR rule while its run isn't terminal;
   - it counts toward neither the review cap nor the conflict cap;
   - the engine refuses to execute or deliver a round of an unknown kind, failing it with a clear reason, without throwing in readers.
2. **Draft deferrals are rechecked on change, not on every pass.** A trigger skipped with "PR is draft" is looked up live about every 60 s for as long as the PR stays a draft (`pendingConflictTriggers`, `processConflictTriggers`). Recheck it only when the poller observes a change on that PR: no longer draft, a new head, or closed.

## Tests (no network)
- A row with kind `ci` doesn't make `reviewRounds` throw. It blocks a new review or conflict round on that PR while in flight, and counts toward neither cap.
- An unknown-kind round run fails with a clear reason and pushes nothing.
- A draft deferral makes no `gh` lookups while the PR is unchanged, and starts its round once the poller sees the PR become ready on the same head.

## Budget
About 40 lines plus tests.

## Out of scope
CI fix rounds themselves (filed separately, after this ships).

Fixes #46.

## Re-scoped 2026-10-09 (M5.5)
The design above predates the landing queue (#388) and review rounds (#360). What exists now:
- Delivery already gets one checked conflict round when the first rebase conflicts (`conflictRound` in `src/pipeline/engine.ts`, tests in `test/pipeline-conflicts.test.ts`).
- The landing queue merges the base into the approved head itself when that merges cleanly, and blocks the entry with `conflicts with <base>` when it doesn't (`mergeBase` in `src/land/queue.ts`).
- The GitHub poller records each tracked PR's mergeability and emits `pr.conflicting` when a factory PR becomes `CONFLICTING` (`src/integrations/github-poller.ts`); `UNKNOWN` is no observation.

So the missing piece is resolving a conflict that appears **after** the PR is open.

## Change
1. **Trigger.** Start a conflict round for an open factory PR when either:
   - the landing queue blocks its entry with `conflicts with <base>`; or
   - the poller emits `pr.conflicting` for it.
   Not for draft or needs-human PRs, at most one conflict round in flight per PR, and at most 3 per PR per day. Record the trigger durably, so a restart neither drops nor repeats it.
2. **The round.** Reuse the existing round machinery (the review-round run kind and the delivery-time conflict round): a follow-up run linked to the owning run whose base and delivery branch are the PR's head branch. It merges the current base into the PR head and resolves conflicts preserving both changes' intent, without widening the change's scope. It then goes through gates, audit and review of the resolution, and pushes the merge commit to the PR branch with a pinned refspec. The PR gets one comment summarizing the resolution.
3. **After delivery.** The earlier land approval covered the old head, so it doesn't carry over: a land entry blocked by the conflict stays blocked with the reason `conflict resolved at <sha>; approve the new head to land`, and a feed item says so. Auto-approving a resolution is the trust policy's job (M6.5).

## Tests (fake `gh`, a local bare repository, the injected clock; no network)
- A land entry blocked by a conflict starts exactly one conflict round; its delivery pushes a merge commit to the PR branch, and the entry's reason names the new head.
- `pr.conflicting` for an open factory PR starts one round; for a draft, a needs-human or a non-factory PR it starts none; a second trigger while one is in flight starts none; the daily cap holds.
- A restart between the trigger and the round's start starts it once.
- A resolution that fails its gates or review ends the round without pushing.

## Budget
About 400 lines plus tests. If it grows past that, deliver the landing-queue trigger first and the `pr.conflicting` trigger second.

## Out of scope
- Clean merges that fail the land check (semantic conflicts) and CI failures: those are CI fix rounds, the next M5.5 item.
- Approving a resolution automatically (M6.5).
- Webhooks; this works by polling alone.

Part of #165 (M6.2 Throughput). Matt chose this on 2026-10-10: the second machine starts by running gate suites, the largest measured share of test CPU, behind one executor interface that the GitHub Actions executor (#310) will share. Design reference: `docs/research/13-cloud-workers.md` §6.2, the executor interface.

## Change
1. **An `Executor` interface in `src/gates/`**, as in research §6.2:
   - `start(req, signal)` returns an `ExecutionHandle` (`kind`, `id`, `startedAt`, optional `url`). The caller persists the handle before it awaits anything.
   - `attach(handle, signal)` re-attaches to work already started, after a daemon restart as well, without starting it again. It returns an `Execution` with `events`, `result` and an idempotent `cancel()`.
   - Gate work uses `Req = { repo, baseSha, headSha, gates, checks }` and `Res = GateRun`. `gates` is the `GateConfig` read from the base commit, as today. `compareGates`, the regression retries and the baseline cache don't change.
2. **The local executor.** Today's `runGates` becomes the `local` executor with identical behaviour: the gate slot, confinement, scratch and process scope, timeouts and events. For `local`, `attach` after a restart re-runs the check, exactly as a resumed gate stage does today.
3. **One path for every gate run in the daemon.** Route these through the executor, reusing one implementation for each:
   - the prepare baseline;
   - the gates stage;
   - post-change and baseline retries;
   - the landing queue's checks.

   `limitless deploy`'s gate and `scripts/land-pr.sh` stay as they are (out of scope).
4. **Selection.** An optional config key, `[gates] executor = "local"` by default. Only `local` exists for now; another value fails config validation with a clear message.
5. **Durability.** Store the handle in the stage's run state, so the resume path knows which executor and execution it belongs to. Runs that predate the change, with no handle stored, resume on `local` as today.

## Tests (no network)
- The existing gate, baseline-cache, land-queue and pipeline gate tests pass unchanged, which shows behaviour is preserved.
- A fake executor injected into the engine:
  - its `GateRun` result decides the stage;
  - the handle is persisted before the result is awaited;
  - a restart between start and result calls `attach` and not `start`;
  - cancelling the run calls `cancel()` once.
- A run with no stored handle resumes on `local`.

## Budget
About 200 changed source lines plus tests. It is a refactor: no new behaviour beyond the seam.

## Out of scope
- The LAN executor, workers, the authenticated LAN listener and machine tokens: the next slice.
- The GitHub Actions executor (#310).
- Agent stages.

Fixes #487.

## What's wrong
Edit-mode agents and gate commands can read the owner's credentials. The outer Seatbelt profile (`src/harness/sandbox.ts`) confines writes and signals, but its only read rule is `denyRead`, and `writeRoots` fills that with `privateReadPaths()`: the SQLite database and its sidecars. The Codex editor profile denies the same paths. Confined readers already deny home directories (`privateReadRoots`), but editors and gates don't.

`agentEnv()` strips factory secrets from the environment and drops `SSH_AUTH_SOCK`, and gates set `HOME` to scratch. Both help with environment variables, but not with files read by absolute path, and `ssh` finds keys through the password database, not `$HOME`.

Measured on 2026-10-10 on unconfined macOS, with main's profiles, `agentEnv()` plus `HOME=<scratch>`, and a one-byte read (`head -c 1`, nothing printed):

| Probe | Codex editor profile | Outer Seatbelt profile (Claude editors, every gate command) |
|---|---|---|
| `~/.ssh/<private key>` (default key, work key) | readable | readable |
| `~/.config/limitless/secrets.env` | readable | readable |
| `~/.config/gh/hosts.yml` (GitHub token) | readable | readable |
| `~/.codex/auth.json` | readable | readable |
| `curl https://example.com` | 200 | 200 |
| `ssh -o BatchMode=yes <LAN host> true` | denied (publickey) | **exit 0** |

Gate commands run the candidate's code: its tests and scripts, and for Dependabot PRs, the updated dependency's install scripts and code. So anything that gets code into a run can read every credential above, send it out over HTTPS, or open a shell on another machine the owner's key reaches. That includes a prompt-injected implementer, a malicious package version or a crafted PR. AGENTS.md's trust boundaries treat that code as untrusted, but the profiles don't enforce it for reads.

Part of #165 (M6.2 Throughput), the slice after the executor seam (#482). Matt decided on 2026-10-10 that other machines join as **discovered, as-available workers**, not as a fixed list. This slice builds the worker protocol and a `lan` gate executor on top of the seam. Discovery over Bonjour and availability rules follow in the next slice; here a worker is given the coordinator's URL.

Design reference: docs/research/13-cloud-workers.md §6.2 (executor interface), §3.5 (infrastructure failures).

## Shape
**Workers connect out to the coordinator, the way CI runners do.**
- A worker runs `limitless worker --coordinator https://<host>:<port>`.
- The coordinator never holds a list of machines. It knows only the workers that are paired and sending heartbeats right now.

## Change
1. **A worker listener on the coordinator, off by default.**
   - Configured with `[workers] listen = "<address>:<port>"`.
   - It serves only `/worker/*` routes, separate from the owner API and its port.
   - TLS uses a self-signed certificate generated at first start. Its key is stored as a private file: mode 0600 and read-denied in every agent sandbox, the same way as the API token (#484) and the credential stores (#487).
2. **Pairing.**
   - `limitless worker pair --coordinator <url>` sends the worker's name and its certificate fingerprint.
   - The coordinator records a pending request and shows a short code. The worker prints the same code.
   - The owner approves with `limitless workers approve <code>` (an authenticated owner route), or in the UI.
   - The coordinator then issues a per-worker token and stores only its hash. The worker stores the token and the coordinator's fingerprint, pinned.
   - `limitless workers revoke <name>` ends a worker's access at once.
   - The pairing route only ever creates a pending request. It's rate-limited and grants nothing until approved.
3. **Heartbeats, every 10 s, with the worker's token.** Each carries:
   - the release SHA, bun version, OS and version, CPU count and RAM;
   - free gate slots, whether the machine is on AC power, and idle seconds;
   - the jobs the worker holds.

   The coordinator keeps a `workers` table (additive migration) with each worker's last heartbeat and capabilities. A worker counts as available only while its heartbeats are fresh (30 s).
4. **Version lockstep.** A worker gets jobs only when its release SHA and bun version equal the coordinator's. Otherwise it shows as "needs update" and receives nothing.
5. **Gate jobs** (a `gate_jobs` table: request, state, worker, lease expiry, result).
   - The `lan` executor's `start` enqueues a job and returns `{ kind: "lan", id }`. `attach` waits for the job's result from the store, so a coordinator restart re-attaches without enqueueing again.
   - Workers long-poll `POST /worker/lease` (up to 30 s). A job goes only to a matching, available worker that is asking for work at that moment.
   - Leases expire after 60 s unless renewed by heartbeats.
6. **The worker runs the job.**
   - It fetches `GET /worker/jobs/:id/bundle`, a git bundle of the head (and base) from the coordinator's repository cache, so the worker needs no GitHub credentials. It imports the bundle into its own repository cache through the hardened git wrapper.
   - It checks out exactly the requested head and records `git rev-parse HEAD`.
   - It runs the request's gate config through `runLocalGates`, with its own Seatbelt confinement, scratch and gate slots.
   - It posts check events as they finish, then the `GateRun` and the checked SHA.
   - The worker redacts output with its own registered credentials before sending. Its token and the coordinator's fingerprint are read-denied to its gates.
7. **The coordinator checks the result.**
   - The result is untrusted data. It's validated against the `GateRun` schema, its SHA must equal the requested head, and its checks must be the requested ones.
   - It's redacted again with the coordinator's credentials and private strings before anything stores or shows it.
   - A result that fails any check is an infrastructure failure, never a pass.
8. **Infrastructure failures**:
   - no worker took the job within 60 s;
   - the lease expired;
   - the worker disconnected;
   - the result was invalid.

   These retry once on another available worker, then fall back to the local executor. They are logged as gate events, never sent to the implementer as feedback, and never turn a failing check into a pass. Cancelling the run cancels the job, and the worker stops it on its next heartbeat or lease reply.
9. **Selection.**
   - `[gates] executor = "lan"`, with `[workers] repos = ["owner/name"]` as a per-repository opt-in. Code goes to other machines only for listed repositories.
   - The prepare baseline and the run's gates use the same executor kind. The executor kind joins the baseline cache's environment hash.

## Tests (loopback only, temporary homes, no external network)
Run an in-process coordinator listener and a worker loop over loopback TLS, with certificates generated in temporary directories:
- **Pairing:**
  - an unapproved worker gets no token and no jobs;
  - approval issues a token;
  - revoking a worker refuses its next heartbeat.
- **A job end to end:** the worker leases it, runs real gate commands from a bundle and posts the result. The `GateRun` matches what the local executor gives for the same commit.
- **Restart:** a coordinator restart between `start` and the result re-attaches and doesn't enqueue again.
- **Infrastructure failures:**
  - a worker that stops heartbeating mid-job loses the lease;
  - the job retries once, then runs locally;
  - no implementer feedback is recorded.
- **Bad results:**
  - one whose SHA differs from the request is refused and treated as an infrastructure failure;
  - an extra check, or a check missing from the request, is refused the same way.
- **Version mismatch:** a mismatched worker gets no jobs.
- **Privacy:**
  - the worker's token and the coordinator's TLS key are unreadable from the gate sandbox (real-Seatbelt probes, `test.skipIf(seatbeltSkip !== null)`);
  - a credential printed by a gate reaches the coordinator redacted.

## Budget
About 450 source lines plus tests. If it runs over, split the work into two PRs: the listener, pairing, heartbeats and CLI first, then gate jobs, the `lan` executor and the worker loop.

## Out of scope
- Bonjour discovery, availability rules (AC power, idle) and a Workers page in the UI: the next slice.
- Whole-run workers, workers that update themselves, and waking sleeping machines.
- Linux workers (they need their own confinement).
- Model logins on workers.


Closes #513

defects.summary: Pairing can't detect a relay between worker and coordinator
The coordinator key and worker credentials are read-denied only while a listener or worker process holds them

# Land checks: retry failing test files once before blocking

## Why
A land check runs the base commit's gates once (`LandQueue.checks`, src/land/queue.ts) and blocks on any failure. On 2026-10-16, load timeouts in known-flaky tests (#556) blocked five landings: lands 73, 75, 77, 80 and 81. Each one re-queued with no code change and waited hours for the single gate slot again. Factory gates already retry failing test files (#548); land checks don't.

Matt decided (2026-10-16): a land check re-runs only the failing test files once before blocking. A pass on that retry lands, recorded as flaky rather than as a clean pass. GitHub CI on the merged head still runs the full suite and must pass before the merge, as it does today, so that is the full-suite confirmation.

## Change
1. When a land check fails, retry only a check that ran and reported failed test files. That is a non-setup check that failed with a nonzero exit code, didn't time out as a whole, isn't a confinement failure, and has `failedFiles`. Retry it once with the base commit's `retry_files` command, the same targeted mechanism `retryFailures` in src/gates/run.ts uses: the same quoting, `validRetryFiles`, and slot rules for small retries. Reuse that code (export a targeted-only helper or add an option) rather than adding a second implementation.
2. If every retried check passes, continue landing:
   - Write the first failure and the retry to the land log.
   - Record the outcome on the land entry, for example the reason text `flaky: <check> (<files>)` kept after it lands.
   - Emit a warn-level event so the orchestrator sees a flaky landing.
3. Block exactly as today when:
   - setup fails;
   - lint, typecheck or another check fails without failed files;
   - the targeted retry fails or times out;
   - the base config has no usable `retry_files`;
   - anything reports a confinement failure. A confinement failure is never retried into a pass.
4. One retry layer, one attempt. No full-suite retry here (CI covers it), and no loop.

## Tests (fake gate runner, no network)
- A test check that fails with failed files and passes on the targeted retry lands. Its log and entry show the flake, and the retry command matches the base config's `retry_files`.
- A targeted retry that fails again blocks with today's message.
- Setup failure, a failing check without failed files, a whole-check timeout, a confinement failure, and a base config without `retry_files` each block with no retry.
- The retry uses the base commit's config even when the PR changes `retry_files` (trust boundary).
- A restart during the retry resumes the land from `checking` without landing on the strength of the unfinished retry.

## Out of scope
- Fixing the flaky tests themselves (#556), the gate-slot ordering (#569), and retries in run gates (#548).

## Budget
About 50 source lines plus tests.

Closes #571

defects.summary: A land retry must require complete failure attribution; otherwise it can land a suite that also failed elsewhere
Normalize the flaky diagnostic before redacting

Delivery: PR reports publish absolute local paths

## Why
Factory PR bodies publish absolute local paths. The implementer's report links files by their worktree path, for example `[hardening.test.ts](~/.limitless/work/<run>/test/hardening.test.ts)` (#576, #561, #546, #528). That puts the owner's macOS username and data layout in a public repository, which AGENTS.md ("Privacy") rules out. The links are also broken on GitHub.

The owner is about to list the username in `private-strings.txt`. After that, every delivery whose report contains such a link would be blocked, so this needs a fix first.

## Change
Before a report or round comment is published (the PR body, PR comments, and the squash body the land sends), rewrite links and bare paths that point into the run's worktree into repo-relative paths: `[test/hardening.test.ts](test/hardening.test.ts)`. Paths under the factory data directory but outside the worktree (logs, scratch, other runs) become plain text with that directory's prefix replaced by `<data>`. Do it deterministically in one shared function, applied at every place where report text leaves the factory, alongside the existing `redactCredentials` boundary. Model text stays data: don't ask the model to fix its own links.

## Tests
- A report with worktree links, bare worktree paths, links to the factory data directory and ordinary relative links publishes repo-relative links and `<data>` placeholders; ordinary links are unchanged.
- The PR body, a round comment and the land's squash body all go through the same function.
- Paths that only share a prefix with the worktree (`<worktree>-other/...`) aren't rewritten as if they were inside it.

## Out of scope
- The contents of `private-strings.txt`. Changing the private-text matcher.
- Rewriting already published PR bodies.

## Budget
About 60 source lines plus tests.

Closes #582

Absolute paths in link labels and link titles are not rewritten
file:// URLs and the canonical spelling of each root are not rewritten

Land queue: a worker that lost its claim can still write outcomes or merge

## Why
Found in #584's review; it predates that PR (the same paths on main).

A land worker keeps its claim with a heartbeat every `CLAIM_STALE_MS / 3` (`LandQueue.process`, src/land/queue.ts), and a failed heartbeat aborts the worker's signal. Between losing the claim and the next heartbeat, the old worker can still act on results it is awaiting:
- a `mergePullRequest` result that arrives after another owner reclaimed the entry: success moves the newer claim's entry to `landed`, failure moves it to `blocked` (`landed()` → `finish()` checks only that the entry is active, not who owns the claim);
- a resumed entry's CI response that arrives after a reclaim: the old worker can go on to issue the merge command.

Reproduction with the existing fake-gh/store helpers: defer `mergePullRequest`'s result, reclaim the entry with `store.claimLandEntry(<repo>, 30000, "new-owner", now + 31000)`, then release the result before the old worker's next heartbeat.

AGENTS.md "Check-then-act across an await" requires re-reading state after an await and making the write conditional.

## Change
After every await in the land path that precedes a side effect or an outcome write (CI wait, merge, push, the fresh merge-state lookup), confirm that this worker still owns the claim, synchronously in the same transaction as the write. A worker that lost the claim writes nothing and issues no merge or push.

## Tests (fake gh and store; no network)

Follows #796. With `[limits] agent_full_suite = "refuse"`, an implement session can't run the full test suite. That stops the duplicate runs and the slot starvation, but the implementer then learns about full-suite failures only from the next round's gate feedback.

The owner's goal: never run the same suite twice. If the implementer has checked the final tree with the full suite, the gates stage shouldn't run it again.

The implementer's own run can't serve as that evidence:
- it runs in the agent's sandbox and environment, not the gate's (#771's in-session suite showed 253 failures caused only by its sandbox);
- the agent chooses its arguments and environment;
- the tree can change after the run.

So the full suite has to be run by the factory, as a real gate.

## Requirements
- **A third mode.** `agent_full_suite = "gate"`. In an implement-role session, a slotted command the wrapper classifies into the gate lane (src/cli/agent-test.ts) is not run in the session. Instead:
  1. **Snapshot.** Snapshot the worktree as the factory would commit it now: the same inclusion and exclusion rules the round commit uses, so the resulting tree hash is what the round would produce. Write it as a git tree object, without changing the session's HEAD, index or files.
  2. **Run the repository's test check as a gate.** Use the normal gate executor, with the test check and setup from the base commit's `.limitless.toml`, the gate environment and confinement, and a gate slot at priority `start`. It runs in a separate checkout of the snapshot tree, never in the session's worktree.
  3. **Record the result** as a gate execution keyed by (run, tree hash, gate configuration hash, gate environment hash), like the baseline cache key (src/db/store.ts `BaselineCacheKey`).
  4. **Return it to the session** as the command's output: the exit status and the redacted output, with the existing failure excerpts. Say in the output that this was the factory's gate run.
- **Reuse in the gates stage.** Before running the test check for a round, compute the round commit's tree hash. If this run has a recorded execution for exactly that (tree, gate configuration, environment), use it as the test check's result and run nothing:

  - the gate artifact and events name the reused execution;
  - any mismatch runs the gate as today. Fail closed: a missing or unreadable record never counts as a pass.
- **Evidence.** A reused result is a factory gate execution, so verify's gate substitution may use it exactly as it would a gate-stage run of the same tree. No result produced inside the agent session ever counts.
- **Scope.** Local implement sessions only. Worker implement rounds and reader roles keep today's behaviour.

Issue #815: Restarts: a local executor runs gates in place, and a restarted daemon re-attaches to them

## Problem
Part of #784 (slice E2, first half), under M6.2.

A daemon restart today throws away every local gate that is running.
- Local gates run inside the daemon process (`localExecutor`, src/gates/executor.ts). Their processes die with it, or are stopped by startup recovery (#795).
- The resumed run starts the gate over, and so does the land check. A full suite here takes 9–25 minutes.
- This is the main reason a deploy drains (median about 9 minutes, up to 45).
- LAN gate jobs already survive a restart: they have a durable handle in run state (`ctx.state.gateExecution`, src/pipeline/gate-execution.ts), a row in `gate_jobs`, and a restart grace (#805). Local gates have none of these.

E1 (#800) made gate and agent-test slots database leases shared across processes, so a second process on this machine can take part in the same capacity. W5 (#795) records spawned processes for recovery.

## Requirements
- **`limitless executor`.** A long-running process on the coordinator machine that leases **in-place** gate jobs from the coordinator's database and runs them. In-place means in the run's own worktree with the existing gate runner (`executeGate` with the local runner), under exactly the same confinement as the daemon uses today.
  - It uses the existing `gate_jobs` table and lease rules, the way a LAN worker does, but marks its jobs in-place. That means no bundle, no push and no adoption, because it shares the filesystem.
  - It renews its leases and records each check's events and result, as worker jobs do.
  - While idle, it polls for jobs with reads only. It runs a write transaction only to lease, renew or report. (#800 needed a round for idle writes.)
- **The executor holds the gate slot.** For each job, it acquires the gate slot itself, at the priority in the request (`GateRequest.priority`), and holds it for the job's whole duration. The daemon holds no slot while it waits on an in-place job. Otherwise a daemon restart would free the slot (#800 expires a holder whose process is gone) while the executor's suite kept running beyond the limit.
- **The gate runs in the environment the daemon keyed on.** The daemon puts the gate environment it computed (the scrubbed `gateEnv()` it used for the baseline cache key, #812) in the job request, and the executor runs the checks with exactly that environment, never its own process environment. Then the baseline cache key describes the environment the gate really ran in.
- **LAN workers and the executor never take each other's jobs.** Workers never lease in-place jobs, and the executor never leases LAN jobs. The gate-job sweep applies its pickup, freshness and lease timers to in-place jobs against the executor's heartbeat. An in-place job that no executor picks up fails over to running in-process, rather than waiting for a worker.
- **The daemon's local gate path enqueues and attaches.** When the executor is enabled and alive, the daemon's local gate executor:
  - creates an in-place job;
  - records the handle in run state before enqueuing, so a restart can find it;
  - attaches to its events and result, through the same `Executor` interface the LAN executor implements (src/gates/executor.ts), as a new executor kind.
  
  This covers the run's gate purposes: the baseline, each round's gates, the targeted retry, and the post-merge check.
- **Re-attach after a restart.** A resumed stage whose recorded handle names an in-place job at the same stage, round, purpose and SHA attaches to it instead of starting a new one. Any mismatch cancels the old job and starts over, as LAN jobs do today. A job is only re-attached while the executor still holds its lease. If the handle was saved but the daemon stopped before the job row was written, the resumed stage starts fresh instead of waiting for a row that doesn't exist.
- **One job per worktree.** No gate starts in a worktree until the previous job there is confirmed stopped and its processes are gone, including after a cancel or a mismatch.
- **Opt-in, with today's behaviour as the fallback.**
  - `[executor] enabled` in `config.toml`, default `false`, keeps today's in-process gates.
  - When enabled but no executor has a fresh heartbeat, the daemon runs the gate in-process as today and logs why.
  - An older release ignores the key.
- **Process ownership is a prerequisite** (#814, which must have landed). Spawn-time discovery rows record their owning process, so a restarted daemon never stops the executor's live gates.
- **Same release only.** Reuse the worker rule (src/db/workers.ts:209: workers lease only from a coordinator on their own release SHA).
  - The executor leases only for a daemon on its own release. When the daemon's release changes (a deploy or a rollback), it stops leasing, cancels its running jobs and logs why. The daemon then runs those gates in-process.
  - The daemon re-attaches only to jobs run by an executor on its own release; any other job is cancelled and started over.
  - An old executor's result therefore never lands under a new daemon's baseline cache key. Handing jobs across releases is E4's blue/green.
- **Land checks are out of this slice** (E2b). They keep running in the daemon as today.

## Tests
Use a temporary database and real subprocesses; never `launchctl`.
- **A gate through the executor:**
  - an executor process leases an in-place job, runs the configured checks in the worktree and reports the same `GateRun` the in-process path produces;
  - the gate artifacts and events are unchanged in shape.
- **A restart mid-gate:**
  - with an executor running a long check, the daemon side is stopped and a new engine resumes the run;
  - the resumed stage attaches to the same job and receives its result, and the check's command ran once;
  - a mismatch (different SHA) cancels and starts over.
- **Fallback:** executor disabled, or enabled with no fresh heartbeat, runs in-process exactly as today.
- **Release match:** an executor on another release than the daemon leases nothing and cancels its running jobs; the daemon doesn't re-attach to a job from another release.
- **Slot:** while an in-place job runs, the executor holds the gate slot and the daemon holds none; a daemon restart mid-job leaves the slot held.
- **Environment:** the job runs with the request's environment, not the executor process's own; a PATH difference between the two processes doesn't change the gate's.
- **No cross-leasing:** a LAN worker never leases an in-place job; an in-place job nobody picks up fails over to in-process.
- **No idle writes:** an idle executor runs no write transactions.
- **One job per worktree:** a new gate in a worktree waits until the previous job's processes are confirmed gone.
- Show that each test fails without its change.

## Out of scope
- Land checks through the executor (E2b).
- The launchd unit, `service install`, `status`, and unloading the executor on a deploy rollback (E2c).
- Agent sessions (E3), deploy without drain (E4), and evals (E5).

Part of M6.5 (the GitHub App decision).

The factory acts on GitHub as the owner: every `gh` call uses the owner's `gh` login (src/integrations/github.ts `runGh`, the `gh` calls in src/git/repos.ts and src/integrations/github-notifier.ts). GitHub therefore can't tell the factory's issues, labels, comments, PRs and merges from the owner's. That matters for M6.5:
- the issue queue trusts a priority label only when the owner applied it;
- the defect reporter's issues must not look owner-authored;
- the owner can't approve on GitHub a PR that is "theirs".

The owner has created and installed a GitHub App for this repository. Its private key is in the config directory. The App ID and installation ID are known to the operator.

## Requirements
- **Config,** all optional, with nothing changing when absent: `[github.app]` with `app_id`, `installation_id`, `private_key_path` (a file path, not the key) and `repos`, the repositories that use the App.
  - The key file must be a regular file readable only by its owner (mode 0600), or startup refuses with a clear reason. Never read the key from the environment.
  - Older releases ignore these keys, because the `[github]` table isn't checked for unknown keys. Say so in the docs.
- **The identity is chosen per repository, by configuration.**
  - Repositories in `[github.app] repos` use the App; every other repository keeps the owner's login, today's behaviour.
  - This is a configured choice, never a fallback after an error.
  - `limitless doctor` checks that every listed repository is covered by the installation.
  - A repository with discreet mode enabled must not be listed: refuse that configuration, because the App's `[bot]` author is a factory mark.

  - For a repository listed in `[github.app] repos`, it signs an App JWT (RS256 from the key file, `iss` = app_id, about nine minutes valid), exchanges it for an installation access token, and caches the token until five minutes before it expires.
  - Every `gh` call for that repository gets the token as `GH_TOKEN` in its environment.
  - For any other repository, and without the config, it behaves as today: the owner's `gh` login.
- **Secrets stay secret.** Register the token and the JWT with `redactCredentials` the moment they exist.
